Signs of the World

Intersection ahead

History

Intersections were one of four hazards that European governments agreed in 1909 to mark with pictorial symbols, alongside bumps, curves and railway crossings. The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends symbols that show how roads meet or intersect.

Adoption

The Vienna Convention specifies two warning shapes. Most of Europe uses triangles. The United States, Canada, Mexico, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and most of Central and South America use diamonds. The same family of signs also warns of T-intersections, Y-intersections and roundabouts.
